capabilityIntro: Remote residential topo and boundary drafting for licensed survey firms. Start with one surveyor-directed sheet and review the editable CAD, plot and source questions against your standards.

capabilities.title: Surveyor-directed boundary and residential topo sheets
capabilities.summary: Assemble a polished residential sheet from the survey firm’s boundary determination, accepted field data and drafting standards.
inputs: Surveyor-issued boundary geometry, annotations and field data
Layer and block library, checklists, sample plot and title-block standards
Contour interval, masked features and licensed reviewer
outputs: Editable CAD with approved boundary, observed features and contours on separate layers
Check plot with spot elevations, labels, symbols and title block
Source-linked questions for the survey lead
checks: Compare corners and labels with the supplied determination
Check contours against ground data, breaklines and masking limits
Document any feature or deed conflict for the licensed surveyor

capabilities.title: Field-to-finish CAD production
capabilities.summary: Turn an approved field export into a review drawing using the survey firm’s code map and drawing standards.
inputs: Accepted point export and field notes
Coordinate system and realization, vertical datum, units and grid or ground basis
Field-code dictionary, figure instructions, CAD template and target version
outputs: Editable drawing in the agreed CAD format and a check plot
checks: Verify column order, unique point IDs and point counts
Match control check values and feature codes against the approved source
Flag unidentified codes and conflicting figure connections for the survey lead

capabilities.title: Existing-ground plans and profiles
capabilities.summary: Prepare topographic base sheets, profiles and contour views from the surveyor’s accepted data and instructions.
inputs: Accepted point groups or surface, baseline and stationing
Directed breaklines, surface extents, contour interval and review limits
outputs: Editable existing-conditions linework and plotted sheets
Requested surface views, profiles or sections for surveyor review
checks: Check the plotted limits against accepted coverage
Route surface, interpolation and outlier decisions to the licensed surveyor

capabilities.title: As-built asset comparison
capabilities.summary: Reconcile supplied observations to prior records and prepare a comparison the survey lead can disposition.
inputs: Accepted as-built observations, field identifiers and asset schedule
Prior record drawings and approved matching rules
Approved datum, units and reporting thresholds
outputs: Working comparison drawing and check plot
Source-linked coordinate differences and elevation table
Exceptions for gaps, conflicts and unresolved asset matches
checks: Preserve record values and observed values as separate fields
Check difference signs and refer each observation back to its source point
Keep a missing measurement blank and flag it for review

capabilities.title: Record indexing and sheet revisions
capabilities.summary: Prepare working files and drawing sheets from supplied records and the surveyor’s instructions.
inputs: Authorized plats, deeds or record sheets
Surveyor-approved linework, annotation and change instructions
Sheet list, reference files and publication template
outputs: Indexed source records and CAD base attachments
Draft sheet layouts and callouts for the survey lead
Revision log and requested supporting files
checks: Match file names, source revisions and drawing references
Route conflicting records and legal descriptions back to the surveyor

formats: Editable CAD in the agreed software version, with references and support files as scoped
Vector PDF check sheets and a source-linked exception register
Point CSV or agreed exchange files for source reconciliation
Editable DXF in the downloadable synthetic examples
requirements: Accepted source revision, point schema, field codes and drawing template
Horizontal reference, vertical datum, units and grid or ground basis supplied by the survey lead
Named licensed reviewer, permitted subcontract arrangement and approved transfer method
boundaries: The licensed surveyor directs field work, accepts survey control and decides professional survey questions.
The authorized survey firm reviews, certifies, signs or seals, and issues final deliverables.
Apply only approved geometry, feature codes and revisions. Hold uncertain inputs for review.

projects.title: Residential topo and boundary check drawing
projects.summary: Convert supplied boundary geometry and field observations into one residential check sheet, with 1-foot contours and a fence flagged for surveyor review.
projects.imageAlt: Sheet SV-401 with the supplied residential boundary, structures, contour lines, spot elevations and S-04 fence review

handoffSummary.Open review: S-04 observed fence relative to supplied boundary

projects.context: A fictional residential survey team supplies approved parcel geometry, local-grid spot shots, a breakline and observed site features. The draft carries the approved boundary onto the same sheet as the residence, drive, pool, trees and terrain.
constraints: Use the supplied four boundary corners and keep the 100 by 130-foot dimensions.
Use the supplied ground point groups and breakline with a one-foot contour interval.
Keep the observed fence geometry separate and refer its relationship to the licensed surveyor.

approach.title: Fit the client’s drawing inputs
approach.text: Keep accepted point IDs and elevations. Draw the supplied boundary and features on separate layers.

approach.title: Draft the terrain and annotations
approach.text: Plot the sample ground shots and one-foot contours with the residence and pool masked. Add a scale bar and directional reference.

approach.title: Flag the discrepancy
approach.text: Carry the fence location as observed and record S-04 for the survey lead’s decision.

deliverables: Editable layered DXF and vector check plot
Synthetic approved geometry, ground point export and review register
verification: Compare four supplied corners against the editable boundary geometry.
Check one-foot contour labels against the sample ground data and breakline.
Check the plotted fence position and cross-reference S-04 in the register.
projects.review: The surveyor reviews the fence relationship and approves the final boundary and topographic deliverable.

projects.title: Coded points to topographic linework
projects.summary: Twelve synthetic observations become labeled roadway features. One unknown code stays flagged for the survey lead.
projects.imageAlt: Sheet SV-101 with two pavement edges, centerline shots, elevations and a red S-01 review marker

handoffSummary.Source: 12 supplied locations with raw field codes

projects.context: A fictional survey lead supplies a local-grid point file and instructions for joining the pavement and centerline shots. The result is a check sheet for office review.
constraints: Keep the original point IDs, elevations and local feet.
Use the instructed figure order and preserve separate feature layers.
Display point 112 as a review marker until its feature is confirmed.

approach.title: Check the export
approach.text: Reconcile the point count and column order against the supplied CSV.

approach.title: Draft the coded figures
approach.text: Join the assigned points as two pavement edges and a centerline. Add point symbols for the supplied inlet and pole.

approach.title: Flag the unknown code
approach.text: Keep point 112 out of the accepted figures and log the decision against S-01.

deliverables: Editable DXF and matching vector plot
Original point export and issue register
verification: Count 12 source records and locate point labels on the check plot.
Check that point 105 remains at elevation 102.24 feet.
Find point 112 on the sheet and in the open item register.
projects.review: The survey lead supplies the missing feature code and approves the updated figure.

projects.title: Existing-ground profile from accepted shots
projects.summary: Five supplied stations form an existing-ground profile through 1+20. The extension to 1+50 stays open.
projects.imageAlt: Sheet SV-201 with five plotted elevations and a held station beyond the end of the profile
projects.context: A fictional survey team provides a baseline and station elevations for an existing conditions review. The sample plots only the accepted portion.
constraints: Use the supplied station distances and elevations in feet.
Label the schematic profile’s vertical exaggeration.
Keep the unsupported extension off the ground line.

approach.title: Validate the station order
approach.text: Confirm the five accepted positions from 0+00 to 1+20.

approach.title: Plot the existing profile
approach.text: Build the draft view and label the elevations from the source file.

approach.title: Record the limit
approach.text: Flag 1+50 for the survey lead to supply the missing shot or remove the extension.

deliverables: Editable CAD profile and matching vector plot
Station/elevation source table and exception register
verification: Confirm that accepted linework ends at 1+20 and includes five stations.
Find 1+50 in the review register and confirm the elevation stays blank.
projects.review: The surveyor determines coverage and approves any interpolation or extension.

projects.title: As-built asset record comparison
projects.summary: Three asset shots are compared with earlier records. One shot plots three feet east and one invert remains open.
projects.imageAlt: Sheet SV-301 with three accepted manhole locations, dashed prior references and a red missing-invert callout

handoffSummary.Source: Prior record coordinates and three accepted shots

projects.context: A fictional surveyor provides accepted as-built shots and a prior three-asset schedule. The comparison keeps the earlier and observed coordinates visible for review.
constraints: Match the three assets by their supplied IDs.
Keep prior and observed points separate.
Carry the missing invert through to the exception register.

approach.title: Join the records
approach.text: Match the asset IDs to source point IDs and retain both coordinate sets.

approach.title: Compare the observations
approach.text: Calculate easting and northing differences and plot the two sets of positions.

approach.title: Log the missing invert
approach.text: Keep the observed rim and assign the unanswered invert to the survey lead.

deliverables: Editable CAD comparison and matching vector plot
Source asset table and coordinate-difference register
verification: Compare prior 62.00 feet to observed 65.00 feet easting for MH-02.
Check that shot 303 stays tied to MH-03.
Confirm the invert blank and S-03 review status agree across the files.
projects.review: The survey lead confirms missing measurements and decides what carries into the issued record.
